$schema_note: Each case specifies an operation sequence against one freshly-registered root agent, run entirely through ONE worker (language chosen by the runner), then asserts on the returned results and final Redis state directly. The point of a *shared* fixture is that the same case, unchanged, is run once per language by test_shared_cases.py/.ts and must produce identical results and identical final Redis state either way - this is what actually proves behavioral equivalence, rather than two independently-written test suites that could silently drift apart in what they each choose to assert.

cases.name: simple_admit_and_full_refund_on_failure
invariants: budget is never negative at any point
exactly one reservation key existed between the two operations
